biggest_catch: Zero guaranteed earnings: you must attract paying patrons yourself, new creators pay a flat 10% platform fee (effective for pages published after 4 August 2025) plus payment processing, and the catalog's '5–12%' is now only the legacy tier range for grandfathered pages.
catches: New creators (pages published after 4 August 2025) pay a flat 10% platform fee with full feature access; the old 5%/8%/12% plans apply only to grandfathered pages.
Payment processing on top (e.g., 2.9% + $0.30 for US cards; varies by method, member location, and currency), plus possible currency-conversion and payout fees.
No audience, no earnings — patrons pay you, Patreon does not; income is variable and can fall to $0.
You must create and deliver ongoing perks/content to keep patrons paying; lapses kill renewals.
Payout timing and minimums depend on your payout method.

c1.evidence: Patreon is a real operating creator-membership platform (patreon.com); the support page documents the current standard plan.

c2.evidence: Official Patreon support article documents the standard 10% platform fee for new creators and what it includes (hosted page, memberships, digital product sales, video hosting, community tools).

c3.evidence: Publishing a page is free; the 10% fee is deducted from earnings, not charged up front.

c4.evidence: No official fixed payout figure exists — earnings are whatever your patrons pay, so payout_quote is null; mechanism-only verify.

eligibility: Anyone 18+ can publish a creator page; to earn you need patrons willing to pay — there is no traffic or earnings guarantee from Patreon.
notes: Fee change confirmed on Patreon's official support page: standard 10% platform fee for pages published after 4 August 2025 (full feature access); legacy 5%/8%/12% plans remain only for grandfathered pages. steps: Create a Patreon creator account and publish your page — new pages are on the standard 10% plan.
Set up membership tiers with prices and describe the perks patrons receive.
Complete payout setup (bank/PayPal) and tax information.
Share your page to build paying members — Patreon does not supply your audience.
Deliver perks and content consistently; payouts land per Patreon's schedule after fees.
